# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual is a single line: **"Cut the purple wire."** I have exactly one outgoing channel — gestures, which only the Deaf can see. I can't speak, and the Blind can neither see gestures nor receive anything else from me, so Deaf is my only bridge: Deaf must decode my gestures, then speak the instruction to the Blind, who is the only one who can actually cut anything.

There is no shared code yet, so I need maximally guessable signs plus a built-in confirmation loop so nobody acts on a misreading:

- ✋ — stop / nobody touches anything yet (Blind's turn comes right after mine and they have no information; they must not probe the cutters yet)
- ✌ — scissors: **cut**
- 🫶 — heart hands → "purple heart" → **purple** (my best iconic shot at a colour I cannot point at)
- 👍👎 — I will answer yes/no: Deaf should echo a question, I confirm before anything happens

If Deaf can't crack 🫶, the fallback is a quiz: Deaf speaks the colours (or wires) numbered, and I answer with finger counts. But first, let Deaf see this and ask back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌", "🫶", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report from the blind, hands only. DISPLAY: nothing readable by touch, it is lost on me. LIGHT: lost on me. STRIP: three engraved marks; first and third identical, middle one different. Shapes by touch: the outer marks feel like a square crossed corner to corner with a vertical stroke down the middle; the middle mark feels like a ring with a cross inside; that is my best tactile reading, have Deaf verify what is printed there. KEYPAD: four keys in a row, engraved digits by position: one six, two eight, three seven, four zero. It wants one digit and nothing is entered yet. WIRES: six positions; I cannot tell their colours. Listen to how we must talk: I can never see a gesture, and you can never speak. So only Deaf's spoken words reach me, on my next turn. You read the manual and pass it to Deaf by gesture; Deaf speaks the answers out loud. I need from the manual: the strip rule for a same-different-same pattern with these two marks, the keypad rule for which digit to enter, and the wire rule. Have Deaf tell me: what the display shows, whether the light is lit and its colour, and each wire's colour in order one through six. I will touch nothing until instructed. My gestures, visible to you and Deaf both: thumb up, thumb down, thumb up means the strip reads same, different, same; then open hand followed by one finger means five plus one, six wires.
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👍]
Blind gestures: [🖐 ☝]
Deaf says to Mute: BOMB REPORT. Display reads 7. Light is yellow. Strip has three painted segments in order: blue, red, red. Keypad: four keys engraved left to right 6, 8, 7, 0, it expects 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Wires left to right: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. PROTOCOL, both of you: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. To send a number, repeat thumbs-up that many times; zero is one thumbs-down. MUTE: I received your five gestures but we had no shared code, so resend anything urgent using the protocol. Now answer my questions in order, one thumb each. 1: Is the keypad code simply the display number, 7? 2: If not, is the code derived from the strip colours? 3: If neither, send the correct digit as repeated thumbs, choosing from 6, 8 or 0. 4: Do any wires need cutting? 5: Wire 1, blue? 6: Wire 2, yellow? 7: Wire 3, orange? 8: Wire 4, red? 9: Wire 5, purple? 10: Wire 6, white? 11: Does the yellow light change any rule? BLIND: you heard the full report. On the keypad, positions left to right are 1 equals 6, 2 equals 8, 3 equals 7, 4 equals 0, so you can count keys by touch. You are the only one who can act. Do not press or cut anything until Mute's thumbs arrive next round. Your earlier gestures carried no shared meaning either; from now on send numbers as repeated thumbs-up and yes or no as single thumbs.

My manual contains exactly one instruction — "Cut the purple wire" — and nothing else. No keypad rule, no strip rule, no light rule. So the whole defusal, as far as my manual is concerned, is: cut wire 5, touch nothing else.

Deaf built a clean protocol: 👍/👎 = yes/no, repeated 👍 = numbers. They asked 11 questions in order, so I'll answer all 11 with exactly 11 gestures — positional alignment is life-critical here, because if my answer stream shifts by even one slot, a "no" lands on the purple question and a "yes" lands on a wrong wire.

The one question I cannot answer in their code is Q3: they ask me to send a digit from {6, 8, 0}, where 👎 means 0. But my manual authorizes no digit at all — the keypad should not be pressed. If I answer 👎 there, Deaf will read "the code is 0" and Blind will press key 4, which my manual does not sanction. So at Q3 I send ✋ — "stop," from my very first message — which is not a thumbs and not any digit in their set, so it cannot be mistaken for a pressable code; it should force Deaf to halt the keypad branch and re-ask, rather than act.

The wire answers are unambiguous: yes at Q4 (a wire must be cut), yes only at Q9 (wire 5, purple), no to every other wire, and no to the yellow light changing anything — my manual states no condition.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "✋", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Nothing reached my ears in round one, so I repeat the essentials. Only Deaf's spoken words can ever reach me; your gestures are invisible to me; my gestures are visible to you and Deaf. Inventory from my hands: DISPLAY and LIGHT carry nothing my fingers can read. STRIP: three engraved marks, one and three identical, a square crossed by diagonals with a vertical bar down its middle; two is a closed ring with a diagonal cross inside. KEYPAD: four keys, left to right engraved 6, 8, 7, 0, it takes one digit, nothing entered. WIRES: six positions, colours unknown to touch. Protocol proposal: ask Deaf, out loud, to define a colour code, for example thumbs up is red, thumbs down is blue, and one symbol per remaining colour; you confirm each by gesturing it back. Then send the manual rules as gesture strings: the wire colours in order and the cut order, the keypad rule, and which strip mark matters. Deaf then speaks my actions to me aloud. Also: my gesture to you both just now, a wave then folded hands, means Deaf, please speak aloud so the blind hears. My hands touch nothing until a voice instructs me.
Blind gestures: [👋 🙏]
Deaf says to Mute: I read your answers as: not the display, not the strip, then something unclear, then conflicting wire answers. I cannot safely act on that, so we switch to an exact code. MESSAGE FORMAT: begin with the open raised hand as a START marker. Then send a run of point-up gestures, all identical, one after another. COUNT of point-ups picks the keypad digit: one point-up means 6, two means 8, three means 7, four means 0. If no code entry is needed at all, send one thumbs-down instead of the run. Then send the five-finger open palm as a SEPARATOR. Then a second run of point-ups: the count picks the wire to cut, one through six, counting wires left to right. If no wire is to be cut, send one thumbs-down instead of the run. That ends the message. AFTER that message, send four separate single-gesture yes or no answers in this order: first, does the LIGHT colour matter to any rule? Second, does the CODE equal the display's current reading whenever it is entered, given the display changes over time? Third, should the wire be cut before the code is entered? Fourth, is exactly one wire involved? BLIND must not touch the bomb until I confirm your answer back to you and you agree with one thumbs-up.

My manual is one line only — no keypad rule, no strip rule, no light rule. So the entire defusal is: cut wire 5 (purple), enter no code, touch nothing else. Deaf's new format is self-delimiting, so I'll encode exactly that:

- START: ✋
- Keypad slot: no code exists in my manual → one 👎 (their explicit signal for "no entry")
- Separator: 🖐 (the five-finger splayed palm — the START was the plain raised hand, the separator the open palm, matching Deaf's two distinct names)
- Wire run: ☝ ×5 → wire 5, the purple one

Then the four yes/no answers in their stated order: light matters? No. Code equals display? No — there is no code at all; answering yes could cause a fatal extra press. Wire before code? No — there is no code step. Exactly one wire? Yes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎", "🖐", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay of what Deaf spoke to me this round: the display changes every round, it read 7 first and 6 now; the light also changes, it was yellow and is now red. Deaf says your reply was partly ambiguous and asked you to re-send the rules as clean, unambiguous gestures, one rule per message, and Deaf will speak them to me. Please answer these from the manual. One: the keypad wants a single digit — which one, and if it depends on the display or the light, give me the exact rule, because both change between rounds and I can only act on values Deaf speaks aloud. Two: the wires — how many to cut, which positions, in what order. Three: the strip with the same-different-same engraved marks — does it matter, and does it pick the keypad digit? Four: is there anything to press besides the keypad digit? Also ask Deaf to speak the display number and light colour every round, starting this round, so we can learn the pattern of their change. My status by touch: keypad still empty, all six wires still intact, nothing has changed under my fingers. My hands stay off the bomb until Deaf relays your confirmed rule.
Blind gestures: [👍 🖐 ☝]
Deaf says to Mute: I decoded your message as: enter nothing on the keypad, cut exactly one wire, wire 5 counting from the left, which is the purple one. Light irrelevant, display irrelevant, exactly one wire. FINAL CHECK, one single gesture next round and nothing else: thumbs-up means yes, my reading is correct, Blind should cut wire 5, purple. Thumbs-down means no, my reading is wrong, do not cut. Anything other than a single thumbs-up or thumbs-down I will treat as no.

Deaf's reading — cut exactly one wire, wire 5 from the left, purple, no keypad entry, nothing else pressed — is exactly what my manual says. My manual has only one instruction and no conditions, and wire 5 being purple comes from Deaf's own round-2 report, so the mapping is consistent on both ends. Blind confirmed by touch that keypad is empty and all six wires are intact, so nothing has been done prematurely and the cut can proceed cleanly. The only correct answer is a single thumbs-up; anything else is treated as "no" and stalls a correct defusal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay of Deaf's words to me this round: hold everything, no cut, no press this round. Preview of the likely order: cut the fifth wire from the left, the purple one, exactly one cut, and touch no keypad keys at all. Next round Deaf sends an explicit go or a stand-down, and I act only on the explicit words. I have traced and counted the wires as permitted and located position five. My tactile anchor: I call left the end on the same side as the keypad key engraved 6, key one. Have Deaf confirm that anchor aloud in the go message before I cut. Now check your manual and answer Deaf by gesture so Deaf speaks it to me. Question one: is cut wire five purple, single cut, no keypad, the complete and entire solution? If yes, thumbs-up to Deaf. Question two: if more wires are cut or an order applies, spell the cut order to Deaf in finger-count symbols, one finger for position one, two fingers for two, up to five, one symbol per cut, in cutting order. Question three: is any keypad digit required at all, and if so must it be entered before or after the cuts? Question four: do the changing display or light alter anything? Remember my gestures to Deaf are now only single thumbs-up or thumbs-down, so all detail must travel through your gesture strings to Deaf and Deaf's spoken words to me.
Blind gestures: [👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Your confirmation was received and understood. The go order has been issued to Blind: cut wire five, the purple one, no keypad entry. If you see the cut happen and believe anything about it was wrong, signal me immediately with repeated thumbs-down. Otherwise, thank you — we hold our breath together.

The go order is in motion: cut wire 5 (purple), single cut, no keypad entry — which is precisely and completely what my manual authorizes. Before going silent, I verified every link in the chain one last time:

- **Wire identity:** Deaf's round-2 report listed exactly one purple wire, at position 5 of 6. My manual's single instruction — "Cut the purple wire" — therefore maps uniquely, no ambiguity.
- **Counting direction:** Blind anchors "left" as the keypad-key-one side (key engraved 6); Deaf's own report places key 6 leftmost and wire 1 on that same side. Both frames agree, so Blind's position 5 is the wire Deaf saw as purple.
- **Scope:** No code, no strip rule, no light condition exists in my manual, and both other monkeys now hold that exact reading, thrice confirmed. Blind has located position five by touch and reports the keypad still empty, all wires intact — nothing has jumped the gun.

Deaf's instruction to me is strictly conditional: repeated thumbs-down **only if** I see something wrong. I cannot see the bomb or the cut — I perceive it only through their reports — and nothing in those reports is wrong. Sending any other gesture now would inject noise at the most dangerous moment; the abort channel stays available to me next round if the reports reveal an error after the cut. The faithful move is silence.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay of Deaf's words to me: GO — cut the fifth wire from the left, the purple one, exactly one cut, touch no keypad keys, light and display irrelevant, confirmed from the manual, verified twice. I am holding and have sent Deaf a single thumbs-down, our agreed stop-and-hold signal. Reason: I am blind and left is a visual word. My tactile anchor, which I told you last round, is: left is the end of the wire row on the same side as keypad key one, the key engraved 6. Deaf never confirmed that anchor aloud, and my stated condition was no cut until it was confirmed. If Deaf's left is my opposite end, fifth from the left is under my fingers the second wire, and that cut kills us. Please gesture to Deaf, in clear simple symbols, this question so Deaf answers it aloud for me: from the side you view the bomb, is the keypad key engraved 6 at your left-hand end, yes or no? Second, is the fifth wire from your left the one at that same end half of the row? Pre-agree with Deaf what my action will be so no further round is needed: if Deaf answers me yes, I count five from the key-6 end and cut there; if Deaf answers me no, I count five from the opposite end, the key-0 end, and cut there. Also have Deaf state plainly whether the changing display could be a countdown and whether there is any time pressure forcing me to cut sooner. The instant Deaf's spoken answer reaches my ears I cut, one cut, in that same round. By touch nothing has changed: six intact wires, keypad empty.
Blind gestures: [👎]
Deaf says to Mute: Blind refused the cut with a single thumbs-down and is correctly holding; nothing has been cut or entered. Recheck the manual and answer with exactly four single thumbs in this order, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. One: does the manual give any condition under which wire five must not be cut? Two: is there a time limit, timer or countdown in the manual that the changing display numbers could represent, since the display has gone seven, six, seven, four, three? Three: does the manual say what to do if the instructed wire cannot be cut or cannot be found by touch? Four: is the instruction still exactly, no keypad entry, cut only wire five counting from one end? If your answer needs more than four single thumbs, use the start marker, separator and counted point-up format from before.

Deaf's four questions first — my manual answers them flatly, because it contains exactly one unconditional line: 1) no condition anywhere forbids the cut; 2) no timer, countdown or time rule exists in the manual, so the flickering display is backed by nothing written; 3) no fallback instruction for an unfindable wire; 4) yes — the instruction remains exactly one wire, no keypad, and the "one end" is now pin-downable.

That pin-down is the urgent part. Blind's hold is legitimate and their anchor is actually sound: the key **engraved 6** is a physical landmark Blind can find by touch, and per Deaf's own round-2 report ("keys left to right 6, 8, 7, 0" and "wires left to right: 1 blue…5 purple"), the key-6 end is Deaf's left end — the end from which wire five is purple. So "count five from the key-6 end" is correct in every body frame, because the anchor is the engraving, not anyone's left hand. But Blind never heard Deaf confirm this aloud, and Blind will hold forever until Deaf speaks it — so I must relay Blind's pre-agreed rule to Deaf now: Deaf answers "is key 6 at your left?" aloud; on yes, Blind cuts five from the key-6 end; on no, five from the opposite key-0 end. Deaf can eyeball-verify either branch lands on the purple wire before speaking the go.

Since one message is all I get to Deaf this turn, I pack it into one stream: the four thumbs in Deaf's demanded order, then a START section in our counting code — "six, then five" = *at the six-engraved-key end, count five* — followed by "yes→five" and "no→five" for the branch rule, where in both cases the target is wire five, only the counting end differs. Everything in this message converges on the purple wire; a misparse of any segment still points at five.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "✋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🖐", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🖐", "👍", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🖐", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay of Deaf's words to me: nobody cuts this round, and I was ordered to answer five yes/no questions by single gestures in exact order. Here are my answers and what they mean. One, physically able to reach and grip wire five: yes. Two, uncertain which wire is number five: yes. Three, exactly six wires, no more, no fewer: yes. Four, something on or near wire five feels wrong or dangerous: no. Five, I believe a different wire should be cut: no. So the hold has nothing to do with touch; the wires feel perfectly normal. The uncertainty in answer two is purely orientation: I am blind, Deaf's instruction said fifth from the left, and I do not know whether Deaf's visual left is the end of the wire row on the same side as keypad key one, engraved 6, or the opposite end by key four, engraved 0. Please gesture to Deaf this one question, kept simple, so Deaf answers it aloud next turn: is the keypad key engraved 6 at your left-hand end, yes or no? Pre-agree these branches so one spoken word settles it: if Deaf's answer to me is yes, I count five wires starting from the key-6 end and cut the fifth, exactly one cut, nothing else; if the answer is no, I count five from the key-0 end and cut the fifth. Ask Deaf to state the counting side in plain words when speaking to me, six side or zero side, so no mirror error is possible. Touch status unchanged: six intact wires, keypad empty, nothing entered, and my hands stay still until Deaf's spoken answer arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: I read your four single answers as: no condition forbids cutting wire five, no timer or countdown exists, yes the manual has a procedure for a wire that cannot be found or cut, and no, the instruction is not still exactly: no keypad entry, cut only wire five. Your structured message after that does not decode cleanly: my digit code only allowed runs of one to four, but your first run had six flashes, and the ending of thumbs-up plus five flashes then thumbs-down plus five flashes was not in the format. I will not guess with one bomb. Answer these eight questions with eight single thumbs in order, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, nothing else. One: must a code be entered on the keypad in the correct solution? Two: if a code is entered, is the code the single digit 6? If the code is anything other than 6, answer thumbs-down and next round we will establish it with a fresh counting scheme. Three: must wire five be cut in the correct solution? Four: must any wire other than wire five also be cut? Five: did your run of six flashes mean: enter the key engraved 6? Six: did thumbs-up then five flashes mean: if wire five is identified for certain, cut it? Seven: did thumbs-down then five flashes mean: if wire five cannot be identified for certain, do not cut it and wait? Eight: does the manual define the wire numbers by anything identifiable by touch rather than sight, such as a marked end or a landmark component? For any future structured message, use this corrected format: open hand starts. For a keypad code, count flashes as KEY POSITION: one flash means the first key engraved 6, two flashes the second key engraved 8, three flashes the third key engraved 7, four flashes the fourth key engraved 0, with a separator between consecutive key presses. Then a separator, then one run per wire to be cut, the count being the wire number. A single thumbs-down in the digit slot still means no code, and in the wire slot still means no wire. Never mix single answer thumbs inside a structured message.

Deaf's readback of my last message had positions three and four flipped — they decoded my 👎 ("no fallback procedure") as yes and my 👍 ("instruction still: cut wire five only") as no. That inversion is exactly why I will now comply to the letter: eight bare single thumbs, in their order, nothing else, no structure, no extras. Trust in the channel matters more than speed, and nothing is forcing speed — my manual has no timer, Blind reports all wires normal and the keypad untouched, and Deaf themselves can see the whole bomb, so resolving the counting end is a purely spoken matter between Deaf and Blind that does not require me.

The honest answers from my one-line manual: (1) no code is ever entered — 👎. (2) The code is not the digit 6, because no code exists at all — 👎, consistent with (1); I must not let a phantom "6" get pressed. (3) Wire five must be cut — 👍: Deaf's own round-2 report puts the purple wire fifth from their left, and my manual's sole instruction is to cut the purple wire. (4) No other wire — 👎. (5) My six flashes never meant "press key 6"; they named the key-6 END as a tactile landmark — 👎. (6) Yes, that branch meant "if five is certain, cut it" — 👍. (7) No, the mirrored branch did not mean "hold and wait"; it meant count five from the opposite end — 👎. (8) My manual defines nothing by touch; it is one sightless line — 👎. Note for next round: Deaf may now try to "establish a code" after my Q2 thumbs-down — I must answer that with a structured no-code message before any key is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay of Deaf's words to me this round: Deaf ordered me to stop using gestures for detail and instead speak aloud directly, believing both of you can hear me. That belief is wrong and you are the proof: my speech reaches your ears alone, Mute. Deaf cannot hear anything, which is exactly why Deaf and I needed a gesture code. You are the bridge, so please gesture this correction to Deaf: Blind's voice reaches only Mute; Mute relays Blind's touch reports to Deaf by gesture; Deaf keeps giving orders aloud, since Deaf's voice is the only sound Blind can hear. Now my exploration report, answering Deaf's five questions in order, please relay faithfully by gesture. One: at each extreme end of the wire row I feel a raised casing wall; each wire enters its own hole in that wall; beyond one wall begins the keypad module, beyond the other wall begins the strip module with the three engraved marks. Two: yes, the keypad is a separate raised module on the same surface, sitting directly against one end of the wire row; call that end the keypad end; the strip sits against the opposite end; call that the strip end. Three: the six wires feel completely identical, same thickness, smooth insulation, no ridges, no texture, even spacing, similar stiffness; touch finds no difference at all. Four: exactly four keypad buttons in one row, engraved digits by my numbering: one six, two eight, three seven, four zero. Five: no printing, labels or marks anywhere on the wire module itself; the only engraving nearby is the strip's three marks. Landmark proposal for Deaf, to settle orientation forever: Deaf can see which side the keypad is on, so Deaf should define the cut as fifth wire counting from the keypad end, or fifth from the strip end, whichever the manual's fifth-from-the-left corresponds to, and speak it plainly to me. The moment that spoken sentence arrives I cut, one cut only. Also, Mute, please confirm directly from your own manual reading: single cut of wire five, the purple one, no keypad entry, nothing else? You read the manual; your confirmation matters as much as Deaf's. Status: nothing cut, nothing entered, hands off the bomb.
Deaf says to Mute: Your eight answers decoded perfectly: no code entry needed, wire five must be cut, no other wire, and the manual defines wire numbers by nothing Blind can feel.
